_source: 2026 coaching staffs verified against team sites and reporting, Aug 2026
_instructions: Rate the person who actually CALLS PLAYS on a 1-5 scale, for how well the scheme deploys skill-position players. Keys are team abbreviations. Missing teams default to tier 3. 'role' is HC or OC — on 15 of 32 teams the head coach calls plays, and rating the titled coordinator instead would be rating the wrong person. Re-check every offseason.

_tiers.1: Poor — rigid scheme, misuses personnel, reactive rather than creative
_tiers.2: Below average — inconsistent utilization, limited creativity
_tiers.3: Average, or genuinely unknown — competent but no clear edge, or too new to judge
_tiers.4: Above average — creative, adapts to personnel strengths, creates advantages
_tiers.5: Elite — maximizes each player's strengths, unpredictable, scheme-driven production

_scale_note: Tiers 1-2 are sparsely used this cycle. 21 teams hired new coordinators and 17 have new play-callers, so most of the league is unproven rather than bad. Unproven sits at 3 with a note saying so — that is information, not a hedge.

ARI.notes: 4-11 as Denver HC, Jets offense stalled under him. Reunites with Mike LaFleur; track record is the concern, not the pedigree

ATL.notes: Followed Stefanski from Cleveland. One year as a coordinator, well regarded, not yet proven calling games

BAL.notes: One season as Bears OC under Ben Johnson. Full autonomy under a defensive HC; designing around Lamar and Henry is a favorable setup

BUF.notes: Deep Saints résumé under Payton, but the late New Orleans offenses declined. Allen elevates whatever is called

CAR.notes: Brad Idzik holds the OC title. Solid, run-leaning, unspectacular for pass-catcher ceiling

CHI.notes: Press Taylor holds the OC title. Johnson's Lions pedigree is elite — creative usage, motion, manufactured touches for RB and slot

CIN.notes: Consistently productive passing game, strong WR target concentration. Reliable environment for the top two receivers

CLE.notes: Travis Switzer holds the OC title and comes from a run-game background. Monken calling it is the reason this is not lower

DAL.notes: Offensive line background, first coordinator role. Unproven as a designer of skill-position usage

DEN.notes: Davis Webb holds the OC title. Payton is a proven pass-game architect; RB usage historically committee-based

DET.notes: Three years calling plays in Arizona, competent and adaptable. Inherits excellent personnel — continuity matters more than invention here

GB.notes: Adam Stenavich holds the OC title. Shanahan tree, good scheme, but receiver targets spread thin by design

HOU.notes: First full coordinator role after passing-game work with the Rams. Well regarded, unproven

IND.notes: Jim Bob Cooter holds the OC title. Steichen has a strong record scheming for both a mobile QB and a bell-cow back

JAX.notes: Grant Udinski holds the OC title. Coen's recent work has produced clear RB and WR1 value; aggressive early-down passing

KC.notes: Eric Bieniemy returns as OC. Reid is elite at creating separation and red-zone opportunity

LAC.notes: Shanahan tree, one of the league's best motion and YAC designers. Freed from head-coaching duties to focus on offense

LAR.notes: Nate Scheelhaase holds the OC title. McVay's condensed formations and play-action concentrate targets in a way fantasy rewards

LA.notes: Alias for LAR — nflverse uses 'LA' for the Rams in its stats files while Sleeper uses 'LAR'

LV.notes: Andrew Janocko holds the OC title. Kubiak brings the wide-zone system from Seattle; unproven as a head coach

MIA.notes: Shanahan tree, strong Houston work in 2023-24. Scheme is good; the roster may not have the weapons it wants

MIN.notes: Wes Phillips holds the OC title. O'Connell is among the best in the league at generating volume and clean looks for a WR1

NE.notes: Long track record, strong slot and TE usage, adapts scheme to personnel. Ceiling depends on the roster more than the design

NO.notes: Doug Nussmeier holds the OC title. Moore is pass-heavy with creative route combinations and historically good TE usage

NYG.notes: Coach of the Year in 2018 and a good Chiefs OC run, but the Bears offenses he led underwhelmed. Genuinely mixed

NYJ.notes: Experienced and quarterback-friendly, results uneven across Indianapolis and Carolina. Steady rather than inventive

PHI.notes: First coordinator role, inheriting a strong offense. Continuity is the bet; no play-calling record to judge

PIT.notes: Brian Angelichio holds the OC title and has a TE background that suggests good tight end usage. McCarthy's involvement is the swing factor

SEA.notes: Shanahan tree with real run-game credentials, but calling plays for the first time under a defensive HC. Upside above this tier

SF.notes: Klay Kubiak holds the OC title. Shanahan is the gold standard for RB and receiver utilization — separation by design, motion-heavy

TB.notes: Two years running Atlanta's offense with mixed results. McVay-influenced concepts, inherits real playmakers

TEN.notes: Elite quarterback developer, Coach of the Year in 2022. Freed from head-coaching duties; strong competence upgrade

WAS.notes: Has never called plays at the NFL level. Quinn praises the preparation; the uncertainty is real in both directions
